redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with failing cases wq1 (house FAIL), wq2 (house FAIL), wq3 (house FAIL), wq2m (house FAIL), but with the working tree's implementation the task's tests do not all pass (SELFTEST FAILED: 239/264 cases passed), so the red is not one the fix turns green - SELFTEST FAILED: 260/264 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, OLDPWD; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; no .npmrc to carry or drop

outcome.technical:
drive-phase.py: new refresh_member_records(ctx, state, task, tree), called in advance() before every member gate. It runs integrate-task.py --project

--refresh-records --json and relays a refusal as a stop. The record set it gets back is stored on state.wave.records. tree_holds_only_integrated(ctx, tree, records=()) now skips paths under those records, so a closed member's tree whose only difference is its refreshed records is still taken down (before this, such a tree was kept). integrate-task.py (NOT in the task's files; the plan gate let the edit through without a refusal): new refresh_records() and a --refresh-records flag. It works through record_paths, the one definition. Every record file the phase HEAD holds is checked out into the task tree, a tracked or untracked record file the HEAD lacks is removed, and `git reset -q -- ` puts the index back at the tree's base. Work paths are never named. run-test-gate.py: task_changed_paths/affected_steps take records; with --tree, paths under _evidence_io.recorded_paths are left out of the member's changed set, so refreshed records do not feed the affected selection. Tests: test_drive_phase.py has new blocks wq-block (wq1, wq2, wq3) and wqm-block (wq1m: a no-op refresh gets no green row; wq2m: a refresh that also checks out src changes the work bytes). In the fixture, P1.1's gate gains check_records.py, which compares the member tree's docs/audit with the main worktree's HEAD; P1.2's gate is red so its tree survives to be read. After the wave is cut, the phase tree commits a task add plus a recorded gate row: manifest, evidence and journal. wt7's mutant lambda was updated for the new signature. test_run_test_gate.py has new rp-block (rp1 records excluded, rp2 the second direction). Separate mutation probe (scratch, module-level mutant): with the records skip removed from tree_holds_only_integrated, P1.1's tree was kept, so wq3 reads it. Runs: test_drive_phase wq/wqm 5/5; test_run_test_gate.py --selftest ALL PASS 533/533; tools/sweep-selftests.py exit 0, 334/334 files ok, 16133 cases; ruff all checks passed; vermin exit 0.
outcome.descriptive: Before each wave member's gate, the drive now brings that member's record paths (manifest pair, journal, evidence) to the phase tree's committed records, through record_paths. Record-only commits on the phase tree no longer turn member gates red, and work files are untouched.

testsAdded: wq1 a wave is cut, the phase tree then commits a record-only commit (a task add), and the member's gate is green: its record checks see the phase tree's manifest pair, journal and evidence
wq2 the refresh touches record paths only - a member's work files are byte-identical before and after it
wq3 a closed member's tree whose only difference from the phase tree is its refreshed records is still taken down
wq1m RED TWIN: a driver that does not refresh a member's records records no green row
wq2m RED TWIN: a refresh that also checks out work paths leaves a member's work files changed
rp1 a member tree's changed paths leave out every path at or under a record path
rp2 with no record paths named, the records are listed like any change
